title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 55-57). Grothendieck is axiomatising 'figures' in his 1986 Analysis situs draft. On the previous page he sets up a poset (𝔉, ≤) satisfying conditions C1 and C2. Its irreducible objects form a set M of 'multiplicités', ordered by ≤ (he stresses: never by <). Each figure F is represented by F̄ = {irreducibles below F}. Equivalently, 𝔉 is a family of lower ('fermées') subsets of the poset M with three properties:
(a) it is closed under taking closed subsets;
(b) it covers M, i.e. every principal down-set M_{≤x} belongs to 𝔉;
(c) it contains ∅.

This page draws the first consequences.

Prop. a) For a figure F, the map F' ↦ F̄' is an order isomorphism from the sub-figures F' ≤ F onto the down-closed subsets of F̄ (closed for the order of M).

Prop. b) Any two figures have a meet: F∧G exists, with closure F̄ ∩ Ḡ. He notes the same should hold for more general families; the margin specifies non-empty index sets I ≠ ∅.

Lieux. A lieu is a minimal element of 𝔉∖{∅_𝔉}. Every lieu is irreducible. Hence lieux correspond to the minimal elements of M, i.e. multiplicities with no sub-multiplicity other than themselves (in effect, atoms or points).

Disjoint figures. F and G are disjoint if (a) they are compatible, i.e. the sup F∪G exists in 𝔉, and (b) F∩G = ∅_𝔉, i.e. F̄ ∩ Ḡ = ∅.

Prop. If F and G are disjoint, then for F' ≤ F and G' ≤ G:
- F' and G' are disjoint;
- F'∪G' is a sub-figure of F∪G;
- the map (F', G') ↦ F'∪G' is a bijection 𝔉_{≤F} × 𝔉_{≤G} → 𝔉_{≤F∪G}. The bijection is completed on p.57.

In modern terms, 𝔉 is a down-closed family of lower sets of a poset M, covering M. This is a 'partial Alexandrov space', or a poset-enriched abstract simplicial complex: when M is discrete it is exactly an abstract simplicial complex. A figure is then a 'face', compatibility means 'the union is still a face', and disjointness of figures says the down-sets split as a disjoint sum of posets. The purpose is to build a combinatorial language of figures, places and multiplicities for the tame-topology / analysis situs project.
errors: No mathematical errors. Prop. a) follows directly from axiom (a): a closed subset of F̄ is in 𝔉.

Prop. b) is correct, and extends to arbitrary non-empty families: an intersection of lower sets is a lower set contained in some member of 𝔉. The margin's caveat I ≠ ∅ is right, since the empty meet would be M, which need not be in 𝔉.

The disjoint-sum proposition is correct. Disjoint lower sets F̄ and Ḡ admit no comparabilities between them, so any lower subset of F̄ ∪ Ḡ splits uniquely as (H∩F̄) ∪ (H∩Ḡ), each part closed. The page leaves the bijection statement unfinished; it is completed on p.57.

ideas.what: Sub-figures of F correspond to down-closed subsets of the set of irreducibles below F
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff representation / lower sets of a poset (Alexandrov topology)

ideas.what: Figure systems as down-closed families of lower sets of a poset covering it, generalising abstract simplicial complexes
ideas.modern_name: abstract simplicial complex / simplicial poset / 'complex of down-sets'

ideas.what: Lieux = minimal non-empty figures = minimal multiplicities
ideas.modern_name: atoms of a lattice / minimal elements (points)

ideas.what: Disjoint figures (union exists, meet empty): sub-figures of F∪G ≅ pairs of sub-figures
ideas.modern_name: disjoint sum of posets; decomposition of lower-set lattices (distributivity)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary order-theoretic groundwork: lower sets, atoms, disjoint sums. Interesting only as documentation of Grothendieck's 1986 vocabulary of figures, lieux and multiplicités; it contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'Lieux de 𝔉 : ce sont les pré[?] figures' should probably read 'ce sont les figures qui sont minimales dans 𝔉∖{∅_𝔉}'.

The end of the lieux paragraph likely reads 'les lieux s'identifient aux éléments minimaux de M : ce sont les multiplicités qui n'ont d'autres sous-multiplicités qu'elles-mêmes' rather than 'qui sont distinctes de ... même'.
In b), 'Montrer [?] pour une famille (finie?) plus générale' is probably 'Même chose pour une famille ... plus générale'. The left margin's 'avec I ≠ ∅' refers to the index set of that family.
Left margin likely reads 'Mais attention : il n'y a pas de raison que pour une famille (F_i) ... ∩F_i ...', a caveat about intersections (meets) of families of figures.
